name: Athletic Training
description: Preventing, assessing and rehabilitating athletic injury, and deciding whether someone is fit to play — a licensed clinical profession in Florida, working under physician collaboration. ⚠⚠⚠ It moved to MASTER'S ENTRY: CAATE states that after the fall 2022 term, baccalaureate degree programmes will no longer enrol students. ⚠⚠ Taught at 8 Florida public institutions, awarding 159 credentials — and 56 of those are still bachelor's degrees.
degreesNote: ⚠⚠⚠ A BACHELOR'S IN ATHLETIC TRAINING IS NO LONGER A ROUTE TO PRACTICE. The Athletic Training Strategic Alliance decided in 2015 to move the professional degree to master's level, and CAATE states plainly that after the fall 2022 term baccalaureate degree programmes will no longer enrol students. Students entering the profession now enter a GRADUATE programme. ⚠⚠ Florida's 2023 data still shows 56 bachelor's degrees under this CIP, all at Florida State — which is consistent with teach-out completions rather than with an open route. ⚠ So if you are offered a bachelor's in athletic training today, ask directly which of the institution's degrees is the CAATE-ACCREDITED PROFESSIONAL PROGRAMME, and get the answer in writing. ⚠⚠⚠ FLORIDA'S STATUTE HAS NOT CAUGHT UP, AND IT READS AS THOUGH A BACHELOR'S IS ENOUGH. Section 468.707, F.S. requires a bachelor's degree from a college or university professional athletic training degree programme accredited by CAATE, plus Board of Certification examination and current CPR and AED certification. There is no loophole — CAATE professional programmes are master's now, so satisfying the statute means holding one — but a student reading the statute alone would conclude otherwise. ⚠ The course file shows the migration mechanically: Florida carries 101 graduate ATR course numbers against 46 undergraduate, and of the 26 ATR courses carried by two or more public institutions, 22 are GRADUATE. ⚠ Note also that the University of Florida awards a professional DOCTORATE in this field, a further step up that is not required for entry.

cips.note: Athletic Training/Trainer — 8 Florida public institutions and 159 credentials in 2023: 76 master's, ⚠ 56 bachelor's (all at Florida State), 18 research doctorates at FIU and 9 professional doctorates at the University of Florida. Master's producers: USF 30, FIU 21, UCF 18, UNF 5, UWF 2.

related.note: ⚠⚠ The closest relative and the comparison worth making before committing to a master's. A physical therapist assistant reaches $68,380 on an ASSOCIATE degree — above the athletic trainer's $62,520 on a master's — and Florida teaches it at 24 institutions against 8 here. ⚠ Different work and different settings, but a student choosing on rehabilitation interest alone should see both numbers.

⚠ The other rehabilitation route, and the same shape: an occupational therapy assistant earns $72,300 on an associate degree. ⚠⚠ Named because athletic training, physical therapy and occupational therapy attract the same students and their credential-to-pay ratios differ sharply.

⚠ Named because the acute side of athletic training — on-field emergency management, spine boarding, environmental illness — is EMS work, and many athletic trainers hold both. ⚠⚠ It is also the fastest way to find out whether emergency decision-making suits you, at 39 Florida institutions and about a semester for EMT.

⚠ Not a route, but a common second direction: concussion policy, heat illness prevention and injury surveillance are population-health work, and athletic trainers move into it. ⚠⚠ Florida teaches it at 8 institutions, all universities, and the master's outnumbers the bachelor's there too.

⚠⚠ A genuine onward route rather than a neighbour. Athletic training is hands-on clinical work that counts as patient care experience, and PA admission turns on roughly 3,200 hours of it. ⚠ An athletic trainer who wants broader scope and roughly double the median has a strong application; six Florida public PA programmes.
